Context: the page is undated. The facing page (78r) holds Vesta orbit reductions for 1807–1809, which suggests roughly 1809, but this is inference. The next page (79) works on theta-type series involving sqrt5. This page is a private exploration of the first-kind elliptic integral written in homogeneous coordinates. Throughout, ' means d/dφ.

(1) Setup (top line). With x = P/Q:
dφ = (Q dP − P dQ)/sqrt((QQ−PP)(QQ−μμPP)) = dx/sqrt((1−xx)(1−μμ xx)).
Gauss writes μ in the x-form and μμ in the P,Q-form; this is a notational looseness, with μ standing for the square of the modulus. The step is checked by dx = (QdP−PdQ)/Q² and sqrt((1−x²)(1−μμx²)) = sqrt((Q²−P²)(Q²−μμP²))/Q². Note added by me: the integrand is homogeneous of degree 0 in (P,Q), so one function of φ remains free (a gauge freedom).

(2) Squaring the defining relation (my factorisation of the right side):
(QP'−PQ')² = Q⁴ − (1+μμ)P²Q² + μμP⁴ = (Q²−P²)(Q²−μμP²).
Differentiating:
2(QP'−PQ')(QP''−PQ'') = 4Q³Q' − 2(1+μμ)(P²QQ' + PQ²P') − 4μμP³P'.
A trial expansion of the left side is crossed out. A further attempt, (Q−P)QP'P'' = (2Q³−P²Q)Q' − PQ²P', is a special trial (in effect putting μ=1 or dropping terms) and is abandoned.

(3) Trial gauge (a pair of second-order ODEs):
P'' = P'²/P + Q²/P,  Q'' = Q'²/Q + μμP²/Q,
i.e. PP'' = P'P' + QQ and QQ'' = Q'Q' + μμPP.
With p = log P and q = log Q this reads p'' = Q²/P² and q'' = μμP²/Q². Gauss writes p'' = e^{qq−pp} and q'' = μμ e^{pp−qq}; this should be e^{2(q−p)} and μμ e^{2(p−q)}.
Other trial forms sit beside these: d(PP')/dφ = QQ, d²(PP)/dφ² = QQ, and the linear trial p''=q, q''=μμp (here p=PP, q=QQ).

(4) Second substitution, p = PP, q = QQ, ν = μμ. The integrand becomes
sqrt(pq)(dp/p − dq/q) / (2 sqrt((q−p)(q−νp))),
and the squared relation becomes
q²p'² − 2pq p'q' + p²q'² = 4pq(q² − (1+ν)pq + νp²).
The middle term is unclear in the image.

(5) Logarithmic form. Dividing the relation in (2) by PQ:
R := P'/P − Q'/Q = sqrt(QQ/PP − 1)·sqrt(1 − μμPP/QQ).
Logarithmic differentiation (with t = QQ/PP, t' = −2tR) gives
R²{1/(1−PP/QQ) + μμ/(QQ/PP−μμ)} = QQ/PP − μμPP/QQ.
Gauss writes the second denominator with μ; the identity is correct. Hence
R' = (p−q)'' = −(QQ/PP − μμPP/QQ).

(6) The same computation in x. Put y = log x, so y' = x'/x and x'y' = (1−xx)(1−μxx)/x.
- From x'' = ½ d/dx[(1−x²)(1−μx²)] = −x[(1−μxx) + μ(1−xx)] (the bracketed terms appear on the page):
  y'' + y'² = x''/x.
- The log-derivative form is also written:
  ddy/dy + dx/x + x dx/(1−xx) + μ x dx/(1−μxx) = 0.
- Result: xx·y'' = μx⁴ − 1, i.e. (log x)'' = μx² − 1/x². The page has trial terms crossed out and ends with 1−μx⁴; the sign there cannot be read securely.

In modern terms: (log sn u)'' = k² sn² u − 1/sn² u. This is the kind of relation satisfied by quotients of theta-type functions, P = θ1-like and Q = θ0-like. Gauss is evidently looking for a natural gauge in which P and Q separately satisfy simple second-order equations, i.e. a numerator/denominator splitting of sn.
errors: Sign error in the trial system PP''=P'P'+QQ, QQ''=Q'Q'+μμPP. It gives (log P − log Q)'' = QQ/PP − μμPP/QQ, but the defining relation forces (log P − log Q)'' = μμPP/QQ − QQ/PP (cf. y'' = μx² − 1/x²). A consistent choice is PP''=P'P'−QQ, QQ''=Q'Q'−μμPP. The system as written belongs to the equation with the opposite sign of the constant structure.
p'' = e^{qq−pp}, q'' = μμ e^{pp−qq} should read e^{2(q−p)} and μμ e^{2(p−q)} when p = log P, q = log Q.
Notational inconsistency: μ and μμ are used interchangeably, e.g. dx/sqrt((1−xx)(1−μxx)) versus QQ−μμPP, and the denominator QQ/PP − μ, which should be QQ/PP − μμ if μμ is meant throughout.
The trial (Q−P)QP'P'' = (2Q³−PPQ)Q' − PQQP' does not follow from the general differentiated identity; it is an abandoned special trial.
Trials d(PP')/dφ = QQ and d²(PP)/dφ² = QQ are mutually inconsistent (they differ by a factor 2). Neither is compatible with the constraint in general; they are exploratory.

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's private theory of elliptic and lemniscatic functions as quotients of entire series (P/Q) is well documented from his Nachlass. This page is an exploratory, partly erroneous attempt at ODEs for numerator and denominator. It reaches the standard (log sn)'' identity but no new completed result.

The homogeneous integrand equals dx/sqrt((1-x^2)(1-mu^2 x^2)) with x=P/Q, since dx=(QdP-PdQ)/Q^2

transcription_corrections: Second item on the top line is likely QdP'−PdQ' or a rewriting of QP'−PQ' (numerator in derivative form), not 'dQP'−PQP''.
'p''=e^{qq−pp}', 'q''=μμ e^{pp−qq}' (with p=log P) is as written by Gauss but means e^{2(q−p)}, μμ e^{2(p−q)}.
'\frac{1}{p}=pp' is likely 'p = PP' (with q = QQ) as the definition for the second substitution.
'\partial\partial p/\partial\varphi^2 = \mu\mu p' probably belongs to the trial pair p''=q, q''=μμp.
The right side of 4pq(qq−pq(1+ν)+νpp) should be read qq p'p' − 2pq p'q' + pp q'q' (the middle term is unclear in the image).
The line 'ddy/dy + dx/x + x dy/dφ = sqrt(...)' consists of two separate statements: x dy/dφ = sqrt((1−xx)(1−μxx)), and its log-differentiated form ddy/dy + dx/x + x dx/(1−xx) + μx dx/(1−μxx) = 0.
The final line reads xx·∂∂y/∂φ² = (crossed-out terms) ... ending in ±(1 − μx⁴); the correct value is μx⁴ − 1.
